_meta.method: Side-by-side synthesis of every key US-vs-China metric tracked on this site, plus the SemiAnalysis Unitree and robotics-supply-chain analyses. The 'Traditional arms vs cobots' section (added 2026-06-18) draws on FAI's 'The State of Industrial Robotics' (Michael & Alden, 2026). Industrial installations, density, stock, cobot totals, selected component and funding rows were checked 2026-10-26 against IFR, manufacturers and original research; other rows keep their earlier capture dates.

bluf.headline: China installs and builds far more robots; the US has more of the AI models and venture capital.
bluf.body: China installed 354,200 industrial robots in 2025, 59% of the world total, and the U.S. installed 38,400, now the second-largest market. The U.S. has strong AI compute and model firms, while China has major manufacturing scale. Components, deployment cost, and repeat orders remain contested; announced humanoid capacity is not realized output.

metrics.us: 38,400 units (+12%) — second-largest market, ahead of Japan
metrics.china: 354,200 units (+20%) — 59% of worldwide industrial installations

metrics.us: 307 — eighth worldwide
metrics.china: 166 — 22nd worldwide using updated Chinese labor data
metrics.note: IFR previously published 470 for 2023 on earlier labor data. The 2023 and 2024 figures are not a same-basis trend.

metrics.us: 393,700 robots operating in factories
metrics.china: Over 2 million — the largest operational stock of any country

metrics.us: Country-specific sales not reported in IFR’s public release
metrics.china: Counterpoint estimates over 80% of ~16,000 worldwide installations were in China. IFR reports about 7,000 full-size (>140 cm) humanoids sold worldwide for professional use beyond R&D and entertainment
metrics.note: The estimates use different definitions and are not interchangeable.

metrics.us: Amazon — 1M+ robots across 300+ fulfillment centers
metrics.china: Distributed across manufacturers; no single fleet at Amazon's scale

sections.title: Traditional arms vs cobots — the AI leading indicator

metrics.us: Not a producer — no US firm makes heavy-duty arms; Adept was sold to Omron, Rethink's assets to Germany's HAHN. Relies on Japanese & European imports
metrics.china: Secondary player — passed Japan in unit production share in 2024, but no Chinese firm tops 2% of the global arm market and median Chinese-firm margins run under 1% vs over 4% industry-wide
metrics.note: Neither superpower leads here: Japan + Europe (FANUC, Yaskawa, ABB, KUKA) hold ~85% of arm revenue. Between the US and China, only China produces at volume.

metrics.us: A few small entrants (Standard Bots); negligible global share
metrics.china: Over half of global cobot shipments since 2023; after Denmark's Universal Robots (~30%), most of the top cobot makers are Chinese

metrics.us: Imports the bulk of its cobots
metrics.china: ~90% of domestic cobot demand met by Chinese makers — versus 55% for industrial robots overall in 2025, down from 57% in 2024 as foreign suppliers grew 27% there (IFR)

metrics.us: U.S. model and compute firms are developing robot AI; most industrial robots in the U.S. are imported
metrics.china: Chinese suppliers are strong in cobots; FAI treats the segment as a possible proxy for future AI-integrated industrial robotics
metrics.note: IFR reports 66,000 cobot installations in 2025, 11% of global industrial installations. A cobot is not necessarily AI-enabled.

metrics.us: Figure ~350 built (1/hour by spring 2026); Agility single-digit units per shift
metrics.china: Unitree 5,500 shipped in 2025 (20K target 2026); AgiBot reported its 20,000th production-line robot in September 2026; UBTECH 1,000+ industrial units delivered

metrics.us: Tesla reported early Optimus production in Q3 2026; a comparable public list price is not established here
metrics.china: Unitree G1 listed from ~$13.5–16K in 2026 reporting

metrics.us: ≈52K/yr design targets: BotQ 12K + RoboFab 10K + Hyundai's planned 30K Atlas plant — plus Tesla's 1M/yr Fremont ambition
metrics.china: Unitree 20K target for 2026 alone; UBTECH 10K/yr by 2027; ~200 humanoid makers
metrics.note: Nameplate targets, delivery targets and production output are different measures and should not be added as realized output.

metrics.us: Agility and GXO report commercial Digit operation in Georgia; expansion to two more GXO sites is expected in early 2027
metrics.china: SemiAnalysis estimated teleoperated Unitrees at ~$23–26/hr in a 2026 analysis
metrics.note: These are different use cases, not a like-for-like cost comparison.

metrics.us: Agility reports commercial Digit operations; comparable robot-level margins are not publicly established here
metrics.china: SemiAnalysis estimated ~67% gross margin on Unitree G1 in June 2026
metrics.note: Different products and reporting scopes prevent a direct unit-margin comparison.

metrics.us: Figure builds actuators in-house; U.S. merchant suppliers include Cone Drive
metrics.china: China has a broad component supplier base; a comparable global humanoid-component share is not established here

metrics.metric: Cost to build the same robot
metrics.us: SemiAnalysis estimated a modeled UR5e-class arm would cost about 2.2× as much to build in the U.S.
metrics.china: The model uses Chinese component and production costs as its baseline
metrics.note: This 2025 estimate covers one modeled arm, not every robot or supplier.

metrics.us: MP Materials began commercial magnet production in 2025; its planned 10X facility targets 7,000 t/yr at full capacity
metrics.china: Adamas estimated over 90% of global NdFeB magnet production in 2025; export licensing began in April 2025

metrics.us: ~5% of global capacity; first US heavy-REE output in decades (Energy Fuels, Mar 2026)
metrics.china: ~91% of global capacity; ~99% of heavy rare earths

metrics.us: Harmonic Drive produces in Beverly, Massachusetts; Cone Drive manufactures harmonic gearing in Traverse City, Michigan
metrics.china: Chinese reducer makers compete with established Japanese suppliers; a comparable global share is not established here

metrics.us: Ouster reported $169M revenue in 2025 across its lidar business
metrics.china: Hesai, RoboSense, Huawei and Seyond held 89% of the automotive lidar market by Yole’s 2024 estimate; this is not a robot-lidar share

metrics.us: Figure builds packs in-house; EnerSys announced a South Carolina lithium-ion cell facility targeting production in 2028
metrics.china: Chinese firms supplied about 70% of global EV battery installations in 2025; that is an EV proxy, not a robot-cell share

metrics.us: Research-grade, low volume (Psyonic; Shadow in UK)
metrics.china: Linkerbot claims >80% of high-DoF hands; 10,000th shipped Nov 2025

metrics.us: NVIDIA Jetson Thor is the de facto humanoid standard — used by Chinese OEMs too; Qualcomm, Ambarella alternatives
metrics.china: Dependent on US chip designs; domestic alternatives under export-control pressure

metrics.us: Physical Intelligence ($5.6B), Skild ($14B), NVIDIA GR00T, Figure Helix — the deepest bench
metrics.china: Fast followers; Unitree is the leading platform for humanoid AI research but the frontier models are American

metrics.us: Figure and Skild drew large U.S. venture rounds; a cited tracker reports over $23B globally for robotics in 2026 to midyear
metrics.china: Older estimates put humanoid-firm funding at ~$769M in 2023 and ~$990M in H1 2024
metrics.note: Different years and scopes prevent a direct country comparison.

metrics.us: Symbotic, Serve, Ouster listed; no humanoid IPO yet
metrics.china: Unitree's STAR Market IPO approved in a record 73 days at ~$6.2B; UBTECH already listed in HK. After its Aug 19 STAR debut Unitree fell about 53% from its first-day high by mid-September

metrics.us: DoD OSC loans + MP price floor (~$3B+ committed to magnets); National Commission on Robotics Act proposed (H.R. 7334 / S. 4686); GUARD Act introduced; House-passed FY2027 NDAA would restrict DoD obtaining foreign-adversary humanoids (Sec. 163); Unitree on the Pentagon 1260H list since June 8
metrics.china: 15th Five-Year Plan approved March 12: robotics as a strategic emerging industry, embodied intelligence as a future industry; AI+ adoption and application pilots; national humanoid standards (2026); 'Robot+' density-doubling roadmaps; MIIT draft (comments closed Sept 23) proposes 100+ humanoid standards by 2028

metrics.us: Quarters — supply loops cross the Pacific
metrics.china: Weeks — proximate suppliers from the smartphone/EV ecosystem

unitree_case.title: Case study: Unitree vs the U.S. humanoid stack
unitree_case.intro: SemiAnalysis calls Unitree the proof of the 'DJI strategy' — bootstrap through researchers and hobbyists, own the bottleneck components, then ride ecosystem maturity into every adjacent market. Here is how it stacks against the American approach, dimension by dimension.

rows.us_oems: Figure 350+ built by spring 2026; Tesla reported early Optimus production in Q3 2026 without a production count

rows.unitree: $50K+ → $27.3K in 12–18 months; under $20K in some deals; G1 from ~$16K
rows.us_oems: Commercial pricing varies by maker and contract; comparable public list prices are limited

rows.unitree: ~67% on the G1 — profitable while cutting prices
rows.us_oems: Pre-commercial; burn funded by venture capital

rows.unitree: Self-developed BLDC motors (30–40% of Western motor cost), planetary gearboxes, lidars, depth cameras
rows.us_oems: Figure builds actuators/packs in-house at BotQ; Tesla designs in-house but buys volume parts from Sanhua/Tuopu (China)

rows.unitree: SemiAnalysis reports a G1 configuration without American components
rows.us_oems: SemiAnalysis identifies exposure to Chinese components in U.S. humanoids; supplier origins vary by product

rows.unitree: The leading platform for humanoid AI research — NVIDIA's open GR00T reference humanoid is built on a Unitree H2 Plus chassis
rows.us_oems: US labs buy Unitrees to train American foundation models on Chinese hardware

rows.unitree: Buys US chip designs; frontier autonomy models are not Chinese
rows.us_oems: NVIDIA compute, foundation models (Helix, π0, GR00T), capital depth, and Amazon-scale deployment demand
